prompted_for: Black-on-white equipment drawing for the service and maintenance page (svc-service), source for art/svc-service.png and the Illustration component
composition: open toolbox with cantilever tray dominant at back
three wrenches fanned in parallel at front left
cartridge filter, sanitary clamp and ferrule at front centre
centrifugal pump with motor at front right
objects spread on one isometric plane with white margins
layout_devices: objects arranged in a loose triangle around the toolbox
line_and_texture: 2 px black strokes, slightly heavier than other art sheets
pleat lines on the filter cartridge
motor cooling fins as parallel lines
motifs: end-suction centrifugal pump with motor and terminal box
motion_implied: spare parts lift out one by one
t2i_keywords: black line art on white background
open metal toolbox with cantilever tray
t2i_prompt: Clean isometric line drawing, black lines on a pure white background, uniform stroke weight, no shading, no fill, no text, no people. A tidy knolling-style still life on one isometric plane: an open container at the back as the anchor, hand tools laid parallel in the foreground, and the replaceable parts and one machine for <CONTENT> arranged around it. Precise mechanical detail (pleats, fins, flanges) kept to clean outlines, generous white margin on every side so the drawing traces into a single-colour mask.
signature_idea: Service shown as a ready kit: the open toolbox, the wrenches and the spare filter, clamp and pump laid out ready for a visit.
strengths: pump and cartridge filter are real water-system parts
weaknesses: toolbox and wrenches are a generic service cliché
pump and clamp read as stainless, not polypropylene
busier than the other art sheets, more objects competing
brand_fit_why: Precise, recolourable line work fits, but the cluttered tool spread and generic toolbox feel less calm and less specific than the brand's equipment drawings.
